segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: I am Rahul, I would like to start the discussion.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: I think artificial intelligence is more of an opportunity than a threat to jobs.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: Of course, AI will replace certain repetitive jobs, but at the same time, it will create

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: completely new categories of jobs.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: If we look at history, whenever technology has changed, some jobs disappeared, but new

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: jobs were also created.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: So I don't think we should see AI only as something that takes away employment.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: Sneha here, I agree with Rahul to some extent, but I think the situation with AI is slightly

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: different.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: Earlier technologies mostly replaced physical or repetitive work, whereas AI can now perform

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: tasks related to writing, coding, designing, analysis, customer support, even decision-making

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: to some extent.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: So the speed at which jobs can be affected might be much higher this time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: A diffier here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: I think we should first define what we mean by, job replacement.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: Because in many cases AI is not completely replacing a person.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: It's actually reducing the number of people required to perform a particular task.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: For example, if a company previously needed 10 people for basic customer support, with

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: AI maybe they need 5 people.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: So technically jobs are not completely disappearing, but opportunities are definitely reducing.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: My name is Priya.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: I agree with that point, and I want to bring another aspect into the discussion.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: The biggest problem is not necessarily AI itself.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: The problem is whether people have the skills to work along with AI.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Someone who doesn't upgrade their skills may lose their job, while someone who knows

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: how to use AI effectively may become more productive.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: I actually disagree with the idea that AI is mostly an opportunity.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: For highly skilled people, yes, it can be an opportunity.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: But think about people working at entry-level jobs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: Suppose a fresher is hired as a content writer, junior developer, or data analyst.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: These are exactly the kinds of roles where companies are increasingly using AI tools.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: So where will freshers get their first experience?

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: That's a valid concern, especially for freshers.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: But I think companies will still need humans because AI-generated output needs supervision.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: Take software development, for example.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: AI can generate code, but someone still needs to understand the requirements, review the

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: code, test it, and maintain the system.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: But that's exactly the problem.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: Here a company might hire 10 junior developers and two senior developers.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: If AI increases productivity, maybe they hire three junior developers instead of 10.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: So even if AI doesn't completely replace developers, it can reduce the number of available

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: positions.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: Yes, but we also have to consider that AI itself is creating demand.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: We now have roles like AI engineers, machine learning engineers, prompt engineers, AI product

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: managers, AI safety researchers, data specialists.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: Five or ten years ago, some of these roles either didn't exist or were much smaller.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: But the number of new jobs may not necessarily be equal to the number of jobs lost.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: Absolutely.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: That's why I said it's not automatically positive.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: The transition period could be painful.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: And there is also an education gap.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: A student from a good college may have access to AI tools, courses, internships, and mentors.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: But someone from a smaller town may not have the same opportunities.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: So AI could potentially increase the gap between different sections of society.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: I think that's where governments and educational institutions have a role.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: Instead of trying to stop AI, they should focus on rescilling people.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: But rescilling sounds easier in theory than in reality.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: Imagine someone who has been working in a particular job for 15 years.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: Are we really expecting that person to suddenly learn machine learning or advance AI?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: They don't necessarily need to learn machine learning.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: That's another misconception.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: If you're a salesperson, maybe you just need to learn how AI can help you analyze customers

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: or automate reports.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: If you're a graphic designer, you need to know how to use AI design tools.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: Reskilling should depend on the profession.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Exactly.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: We shouldn't tell everyone, learn AI or you will lose your job.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: The idea should be, learn how AI can improve the work you already do.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: But companies might still prefer someone who can do the work with AI over someone who can't.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Of course.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: That's why individuals also have responsibility.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: We can't completely depend on companies or governments.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: There's another issue I'd like to raise, quality.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: AI can generate content very quickly, but fast doesn't always mean good.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: There are problems with hallucinations, incorrect information, bias, and lack of context.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: Yes, and that's why human judgment remains important.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: And how much human judgment?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: If AI becomes accurate enough, companies will naturally try to reduce costs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: Companies always try to reduce costs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: That's not something that started with AI.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: Automation has been doing that for decades.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: But AI makes automation available to almost every industry.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: True.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: That's why I think we shouldn't underestimate the impact.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: I don't think anyone is underestimating it.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: I'm saying the impact will depend on how we manage the transition.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Can I add something here?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: We are mostly discussing white collar jobs.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: What about jobs like teachers, doctors, lawyers, journalists, and managers?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: AI can assist them, but completely replacing them is much more complicated because these

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: professions involve trust and human interaction.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: I agree, especially in healthcare.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: You may have an AI system that can detect a disease from an image, but a patient still

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: wants a doctor to explain what's happening and what treatment options they have.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: But eventually people might trust AI if it becomes more accurate than humans.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Maybe for certain decisions.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: But trust isn't only about accuracy.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Suppose you're sitting in a hospital and you've just received bad news.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: You don't want a machine to simply give you a probability.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: You want someone who understands your emotions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: That's a very important distinction.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: Some jobs aren't valuable only because of the task they perform.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: They're valuable because of the human relationship involved.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: Exactly.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: And that could actually make human skills more valuable, communication, empathy, leadership,

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: creativity, negotiation.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: So maybe the real question isn't whether AI will replace humans, but which humans will

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: be replaced by humans who know how to use AI.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: That's a good statement, but I would modify it slightly.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: People who know how to use AI will probably have an advantage over people who don't.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: But that doesn't mean everyone can simply learn one AI tool and be safe.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: Yes, because tools keep changing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: Today you learn one tool, tomorrow another one becomes popular.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: So instead of learning only tools, people should develop fundamentals.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: Completely agree.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: For example, a programmer shouldn't only learn how to use an AI coding assistant.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: They should understand programming concepts, system design, databases, debugging, and architecture.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: Then AI becomes a productivity tool rather than something they completely depend on.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: The same applies to students.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: If students use AI to complete every assignment without understanding anything, they make it

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: good marks but eventually struggle in an actual job.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: That's already happening.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: Yes, and that's actually one of the threats of AI that doesn't get enough attention,

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: the dependency problem.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: I want to bring up one more point, productivity.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: Suppose AI allows one employee to do the work of three employees.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: Ideally, companies could use that extra productivity to create new products and expand their business.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: Ideally, is the important word there.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: Companies may simply keep one person and remove two positions.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: That's possible, but increased productivity can also reduce costs and create new businesses

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: and jobs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: True, but the transition can still be difficult for people who lose their jobs.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: I think both points are valid.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: That's why restilling and proper support are important.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: And for students, the best approach is to learn how to work with AI rather than compete

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: against it.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: So I think we can say that AI is neither completely an opportunity nor completely a threat.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: It depends on how we adapt to it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_C
segments.text: People who continuously improve their skills will have a better chance of benefiting from AI.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_E
segments.text: And companies and governments also need to support people during this transition.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Exactly.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: AI will definitely change the job market, but if we prepare properly, the benefits can outweigh the risks.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: I agree.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: So, in conclusion, AI should be treated as a tool to enhance human abilities, not simply

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: as a replacement for humans.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: I agree.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: Same here.

segments.speaker: Rahul
segments.text: Agreed.

segments.speaker: Sneha
segments.text: Yes.
